speaker: narrator
text: Act I: The Call to Adventure

speaker: narrator
text: You are Elior, a farmer boy in the village of Willowbrook, on the outskirts of Eldoria. Your grandmother raised you after your parents vanished, and your days are the crops, the hens and the weather.

speaker: narrator
text: Tonight the weather is a storm, and a light that is not lightning has split the sky over the fields. Sleep, when it comes, is not quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: Let's get started! (Type 'help' for a list of commands.)

speaker: narrator
text: Dark, and a storm in it. Rain drives against shutters you cannot see, and the thunder comes so close that the dark itself shakes. Shadows move through it the way smoke moves. A hand, a man’s hand, lifts a child out of the dark and holds it against a shoulder, and then the dark has them both. Somewhere a slow tune climbs three notes and settles home again. Among the shadows a figure stands, tall and without a face, too far to reach and too near to be anything but real. Its whisper is at the edge of hearing, and it is your name.

speaker: narrator
text: You answer it. You do not know with what: your own name back, or the question under it.

speaker: narrator
text: The whisper comes once more, closer than the thunder, and this time there are words in it: …and let them rest… Then your name, and the dark lets go of you.

speaker: narrator
text: You wake in your own bed. The storm is gone and there is grey morning in the curtains. Your heart is going hard. The tune is still going too, thin and near: someone is humming it, out by the hearth. Three words are already slipping, and you write them down before they can go.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior dreams of a shadowy figure lurking in the fields, its presence felt even in the waking world. The dream is unsettling, leaving him with a sense of foreboding that something is wrong in Willowbrook.

speaker: narrator
text: After a strange, vivid dream, you awaken with the sense that something beyond the ordinary is calling to you. A mysterious force stirs within, urging you to pay attention to the signs around you and discover what this new feeling means.

speaker: narrator
text: A modest cottage with a straw roof and a cozy hearth. The scent of fresh bread and old books fills the air. Sunlight filters through lace curtains, illuminating shelves lined with trinkets and memories. A sturdy wooden table sits in the center, and a gentle fire crackles in the hearth. Grandmother hums softly in her rocking chair, her eyes twinkling with wisdom and warmth.

speaker: grandmother
text: Oh, Elior, my dear. The village... it feels a bit on edge lately, doesn't it? Willowbrook has always been a peaceful place. The Village Square is usually bustling, though folks seem more hushed these days. If you're needing anything, the General Store usually has a bit of everything. Old Man Hemlock, the shopkeeper, sees and hears a lot, too. And if it's wisdom or a remedy you seek, Mira in her hut to the north of the square is the one to talk to. She has a way with herbs and... other things. The Blacksmith down by the south end, he's a sturdy fellow, always hammering away. Keeps the tools sharp, and his spirits, mostly. Just... be observant, child. There's more to this world than meets the eye. And you, Elior, you have a good heart. Remember that.

speaker: grandmother
text: It's good to see you, Elior. Is there something you need?

speaker: narrator
text: The ink is slightly smudged on this page, as if written in haste or with a trembling hand...

speaker: elior
text: What a night. The wind howled like a hungry wolf, and rain lashed against the shutters. I swear the whole cottage shook with each thunderclap. Sleep was impossible for hours. Then, through a gap in the curtains, I saw it – a searing, unnatural light that split the sky. It wasn't lightning; it was... different. Pulsating, almost. When I finally drifted off, the dreams came. Not the usual ones of fields and harvests. This was dark, filled with swirling shadows. And a figure, tall and indistinct, its voice a whisper on the edge of hearing, yet it felt like it was calling my name. Elior... I woke with a start, my heart pounding. And three words at the very end, which I wrote down the moment I woke so I would not lose them: …and let them rest… Even now, the memory sends a shiver down my spine. And the strangest thing — I knew that voice. Not the way you know a neighbour's, but the way you know a song someone sang to you before you had words for it. It made my chest ache. I just can't remember from where. What did it mean?

speaker: narrator
text: She is humming at the hearth when you come in: a slow tune that climbs three notes and settles home again. You know it. You have known it all your life, and you could not say from where. She stops when she sees your face.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her about the dream: the shadows, the figure, the voice calling your name, and how you were sure you had heard it before. She reaches for your hand and holds it tighter than she means to.

speaker: grandmother
text: That voice... did it say anything more? Anything but your name?

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her the three words you caught at the very end, the ones you wrote down before they could go: let them rest. She goes quiet. She turns to the bread on the board and does not turn back for a while.

speaker: grandmother
text: Some voices are older than memory.

speaker: grandmother
text: That journal of yours... your father was a great writer, you know. He wrote of many things, some of which I am only now beginning to understand. He sensed a darkness, a shadow stretching over Eldoria, long before others did. He believed it was tied to the old tales, to the whispers of forgotten magic. He even researched a peculiar enchantment, one that could supposedly breathe life back into things on the very brink... a 'revive' spell, he called it. He thought it might be a key, a way to mend what the encroaching darkness sought to break. Keep your eyes open, Elior. What you've read might be more than just stories.

speaker: narrator
text: You discover that you possess mysterious magical abilities. Strange phenomena begin to occur around you, hinting at a power you never knew you had. You must seek guidance and understanding to unlock the secrets of your newfound magic and learn what it means for your destiny.

speaker: narrator
text: You have discovered that the strange feeling within you is the first sign of something magical. Your journey into the unknown has truly begun.

speaker: narrator
text: You search the cottage thoroughly and discover a faded photograph hidden in a drawer.

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere in the cottage lies an old photograph of your parents, tucked away in a drawer. Read the cryptic message on its back and show it to your grandmother. Then seek the truth where the river bends.

speaker: narrator
text: Seek the truth where the river bends.

speaker: narrator
text: She studies the back of the photograph, her expression growing serious.

speaker: grandmother
text: You found the message, then? Your parents... they were involved in something much bigger than any of us realized. There is a darkness in Eldoria, and your family is tied to it. There is a secret, Elior — a truth you must uncover. Promise me you'll be careful.

speaker: narrator
text: She hands the photograph back.

speaker: grandmother
text: Your mother loved the river. If anyone remembers what she did there, it's the old fisherman down at the Riverbank.

speaker: narrator
text: You are encouraged to explore and get to know every corner of Willowbrook. The village holds many secrets for you to discover.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior has witnessed the devastation firsthand: once lush rows of crops now stand wilted and brown, their leaves curled and brittle. The earth beneath his feet is cracked and dry, and the air is thick with the scent of decay. Where there was once the promise of a bountiful harvest, there is now only ruin.

speaker: narrator
text: Rows of withered crops stretch beneath a brooding gray sky. The earth is cracked and dry, with only a few stubborn carrots and a rusty hoe hinting at better days. A faint breeze rustles the brittle leaves, carrying the scent of soil and distant rain. The field feels quiet, as if holding its breath, waiting for a touch of magic to bring it back to life.

speaker: narrator
text: It lands heads up. Seems like a regular coin, perhaps for trading.

speaker: narrator
text: A small wooden coop stands here, its planks patched and weathered. Nervous chickens cluck and flutter, their feathers ruffled as they dart between straw nests. The air is thick with the scent of hay and the occasional squawk. Sunbeams slip through the slats, casting striped shadows on the dirt floor. High on a rafter, out of reach, something glints where no hen could have put it.

speaker: narrator
text: They peck at it excitedly, and in the flapping commotion something shiny is knocked from a high rafter. It's a small key, hidden up there long ago by someone who did not want it found!

speaker: grandmother
text: So the chickens gave up my little secret. I tucked that key up in the coop rafters years ago. It opens the old shed by the mill. It was a workshop once... your father's. I never could bring myself to go in. It's dark as a cellar in there, dear; take the lantern with you.

speaker: narrator
text: The heart of Willowbrook bustles with life. Cobblestone paths radiate from an old stone fountain, and a weathered notice board stands nearby, covered in faded announcements. Children chase each other around market stalls, and the air is filled with laughter, gossip, and the scent of fresh bread. The square is a crossroads for villagers, travelers, and secrets alike.

speaker: tilda
text: Have you seen the fields lately? The crops are withering overnight, and no one knows why. It's like the land itself is sick...

speaker: narrator
text: Villagers speak in hushed tones of strange happenings: animals refusing to leave their shelters, and shadows moving where none should be. Elior senses the fear growing among his neighbors, and the mystery deepens.

speaker: tilda
text: Last night, someone spotted a cloaked stranger near the old well, asking after an old amulet, from a family that left. Nobody would tell him a thing, and he took the road to the mill.

speaker: narrator
text: An old stone well stands at the village's center, its stones worn smooth by countless hands. The water below lies dark and still, and a faint sour smell hangs in the cool, damp air. Moss creeps up the sides. The well seems to whisper secrets to those who listen closely.

speaker: narrator
text: Rumors spread of the village well: a foul stench rising from its depths, and water that no one dares to drink. Elior wonders if the source of the corruption lies beneath the surface.

speaker: narrator
text: A hot, smoky forge glows with the light of burning coals. The clang of hammer on anvil echoes through the air, mingling with the scent of molten metal and sweat. Tools and half-finished weapons hang from the walls, and the blacksmith wipes his brow, his arms corded with muscle. Sparks dance in the gloom, and the heat is almost overwhelming.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Well met, young one. I am Borin, the village blacksmith. If you need tools made or mended, I'm your man. A sharp blade can be a good friend.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Welcome back, young Elior. Need something else?

speaker: narrator
text: The blacksmith takes your coin and your dull knife. He expertly sharpens it on his whetstone and hands you back a gleaming sharp knife!

speaker: blacksmith
text: How is that blade holding up? Keep that edge oiled, mind, or the damp will have it dull again before you know it.

speaker: narrator
text: Old Man Hemlock has shut the General Store until his cat, Patches, comes home. She was last seen near the old well, where a locked shed keeps its secrets. What will you discover if you find a way inside?

speaker: narrator
text: A rickety shed leans precariously at the edge of Willowbrook, its weathered boards creaking in the wind. Rusty tools and broken crates are scattered about a long workbench, and a thick layer of dust covers everything. Little light gets past the grimy boards; shadows gather in the corners, and the air smells of old earth and forgotten secrets. Something about the place feels both forlorn and mysteriously inviting.

speaker: narrator
text: You take a look around the shed. Nothing! The Shed Door is locked so you can't search inside.

speaker: narrator
text: In the gloom you make out an old workbench and a few interesting things. From the shadows comes a frightened mew, and a small patchwork shape bolts behind the broken crates.

speaker: narrator
text: A pair of green eyes blinks in the dark. With a small, uncertain mew, Patches creeps out, sniffs your fingers and lets you scoop her up. She is thin and dusty, but unhurt.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches was hiding in the Abandoned Shed. Carry her home to Old Man Hemlock at the General Store.

speaker: narrator
text: Holding the lantern high, you rummage through the clutter of rusty tools and broken crates. Tucked away in dusty corners, you find a discarded Fishing Rod, and a small Magnet!

speaker: narrator
text: Patches peers out of your arms, and your grandmother reaches out to scratch her ears.

speaker: grandmother
text: Hemlock's Patches! The poor wee thing, she's all dust and bones. She's taken to you, hasn't she? With you off on the road soon, this cottage will be terribly quiet. If you'd have her stay with me, you need only say so, and I'll square it with Hemlock myself. Or carry her home to him; he'll be worried sick.

speaker: narrator
text: A fragrant hut filled with drying herbs and mysterious potions. Shelves overflow with bottles, roots, and colorful flowers. The air is thick with the scent of lavender and sage. Sunlight streams through stained glass, painting the walls in shifting hues. Mira herself moves gracefully among her concoctions, her eyes bright with knowledge and kindness.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira smiles warmly as you enter her fragrant hut.

speaker: mira
text: Welcome, Elior. I sense a stirring of the old powers within you. What brings you to my door?

speaker: narrator
text: You describe to Mira the withered crops, the villagers' fears, and the foul stench from the well. Her expression grows troubled as she listens.

speaker: mira
text: These are signs of a darkness that has long slumbered beneath Willowbrook,

speaker: narrator
text: she says sadly.

speaker: mira
text: The land is suffering, and so are its people. But there is hope, Elior. You must connect with the living world—listen to the wind, the water, the roots beneath your feet. Only by understanding the magic of nature can you hope to confront what is coming.

speaker: mira
text: A Rare Flower grows in the Hidden Glade. Seek it out, and pay close attention to the well and the glade; they may hold secrets vital to your quest.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira has urged Elior to connect with the living world and learn from its magic. The path forward is uncertain, but hope stirs in the heart of Willowbrook.

speaker: narrator
text: A cluttered shop overflowing with goods of every kind. Shelves groan under the weight of rope, apples, matches, and trinkets. The shopkeeper bustles about, dusting jars and chatting with customers. The air is thick with the mingled scents of fruit, wax, and old wood. Every corner seems to hold a new surprise, and the promise of a good bargain.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches butts her head against the Shopkeeper's hand, and his face lights up.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Patches! You found her! Old Hemlock won't forget this. Here, the reward I promised. It isn't much, but it's honestly given. And the store's open again, so have a look around.

speaker: narrator
text: Patches curls up beside the till and begins to purr.

speaker: narrator

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Hold on there, friend! That rope is merchandise, not a free sample. If you want it, you'll need to buy it proper-like.

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Hold on there, friend! Those matches are set aside for the priest. He gets them on the house whenever he asks.

speaker: narrator
text: You carried Patches home to Old Man Hemlock, and the General Store is open again. Curiosity did not kill this cat after all.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shopkeeper says:

speaker: shopkeeper
text: Welcome to my humble store! Finest goods in Willowbrook, I assure you. I have a few things for sale: - Rope: 1 coin(s) - Sword: 5 coin(s) - Armor: 10 coin(s) And remember, you always get an extra apple with every purchase!

speaker: narrator
text: Patches blinks at you slowly from the counter and begins to purr.

speaker: narrator
text: A creaky windmill towers above, its sails turning slowly in the breeze. Dusty gears and cobwebs fill the interior, and the scent of flour hangs in the air. Sunlight streams through broken windows, illuminating sacks of grain and a heavy millstone. Amidst the old workings, you notice a strange mechanism of black iron, whirring to itself, that doesn't belong to the mill's original design.

speaker: narrator
text: You thread the rope through the gears of the strange mechanism and pull it tight. The gears grind, catch, and jam. The whirring dies, and the hum in the floorboards fades away, as whatever it was drawing from beneath the mill is left in peace.

speaker: narrator
text: With a clunk, a hidden compartment slides open, revealing a fragment of the old millstone!

speaker: narrator
text: The blacksmith takes the millstone fragment, turning it over in his calloused hands.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Aye, this is from the old mill, alright. Sturdy stone. You know, old tales say the mill was built on a place of ancient power. Some say a magical deer sometimes appears in the Hidden Glade, but only when all is calm and restful—no voices, no footsteps, just the hush of the wind and the song of the stream. If you seek the deer, go there and sit quiet a while; have a rest, and let it come to you. It will not show itself to those who rush or bring trouble.

speaker: narrator
text: You have heard tales of a magical deer from the Blacksmith. Perhaps you will witness something extraordinary yourself!

speaker: narrator
text: A gentle river flows past the village. Reeds sway along the banks, and the air is alive with the hum of insects. A weathered fisherman sits nearby, humming a quiet tune. The riverbank is peaceful, a place where time seems to slow and worries drift away.

speaker: narrator
text: The fisherman notices your fishing rod.

speaker: fisherman
text: Ah, a fellow angler! My arm's busted, can't fish myself. But I can tell you a thing or two. Cast your line near the reeds, that's where they like to hide. Patience is key, my friend, patience.

speaker: narrator
text: He teaches you the basics of fishing.

speaker: narrator
text: You can't help but feel sorry for the fisherman—he seems troubled and in need of help. Perhaps if you assist him, you'll uncover something important.

speaker: narrator

speaker: fisherman

speaker: narrator

speaker: narrator

speaker: fisherman
text: Ah, a fine catch! Thank you kindly. It's been a while since I've had a fresh river fish.

speaker: fisherman
text: The river's water... it's not been right. Murky. Your mother taught me this, by the bend. I reckon it's yours more than mine. With this, you can cleanse water,

speaker: narrator
text: You have helped the fisherman and learned something new about the world around you. Your kindness is rewarded.

speaker: narrator

speaker: fisherman
text: The river has many moods. Treat it with respect, and it might share its secrets with you.

speaker: narrator
text: The fisherman turns the photograph over and reads the back. For a long while he says nothing.

speaker: fisherman
text: Where the river bends... that's here, lad. This very spot. Your mother came to the bend near every evening. Said the water here was old, older than the village, and it had things to teach.

speaker: narrator
text: He hands the photograph back.

speaker: fisherman
text: The night before she went away, she pressed a little tin into the mud under that smooth stone yonder, and made me promise to watch over it. Said if her boy ever came asking, he'd know where to look. I reckon you've come asking.

speaker: narrator
text: You tip the smooth stone aside and dig into the cold mud beneath it. Your fingers close on a small tin, sealed with wax. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, lies a mother's letter.

speaker: mother
text: My dearest Elior, if you are reading this, you found the bend, as I knew you would. The river remembers what the village forgets. If Malakar comes asking about our line, do not answer him. He is not the friend we knew. Mira keeps the amulet for you. When you are ready, it will know you. Your father and I

speaker: narrator
text: At the river bend you found your mother's letter, hidden beneath the smooth stone. Its words raise more questions than they answer, but they are hers.

speaker: narrator
text: A winding path snakes into the heart of the woods, dappled sunlight flickering through the canopy above. A section of the path is blocked by thick, thorny vines. The air is alive with the scent of pine and wildflowers, and the ground is soft with moss and fallen leaves. Birds flit between branches, and the occasional snap of a twig hints at unseen creatures nearby. The path feels ancient, as if it remembers every footstep that has ever passed this way.

speaker: narrator
text: You wipe the blade on the moss and keep it; it may yet be useful.

speaker: narrator
text: A fox kit, no bigger than a cat, one hind leg caught fast in the wire. It watches you and does not struggle.

speaker: narrator
text: A hushed clearing hidden deep within the forest, dim and overgrown. Brambles crowd its edges, and the tall grass stands grey and still beneath branches that shut out the sun. In the center, a mossy stone bears a faint inscription, too deep in shadow to read. An unnatural darkness lingers here, as if the glade itself is waiting to be enlightened.

speaker: narrator
text: You take a moment to rest in the tranquil glade. As you relax, a graceful Deer emerges into the glade. It gazes at you with deep, ancient eyes, and for a moment, you feel a surge of gentle magical energy flow through your body, as if the glade itself is welcoming you. You notice a rare, beautiful Rare Flower blooming near the mossy stone.

speaker: narrator
text: You have observed the magical deer, gaining a deeper understanding of the wonders and mysteries of Eldoria.

speaker: narrator
text: It does not answer, not in words. Its dark eyes hold yours for a long moment. Then its gaze drifts to the mossy stone and the shadowed runes upon it... then to you, patient, as if waiting for you to bring something to light.

speaker: narrator
text: Its dark eyes hold yours for a long moment. Then its gaze drifts to the mossy stone and the shadowed runes upon it... then to you, patient, as if waiting for you to bring something to light.

speaker: narrator
text: A small stone chapel stands in quiet dignity, its stained glass windows casting rainbows across the worn pews. The air is cool and still, filled with the faint scent of candle wax and old parchment. A kindly priest tends to the altar, offering blessings and words of comfort. Over the door a shape is cut into the stone, worn almost smooth. A dark corner by the altar swallows the light.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest offers a serene smile.

speaker: priest
text: Welcome, child. The chapel is a sanctuary for all who seek peace. The shadows in our land grow long, but faith can be a guiding light.

speaker: narrator
text: He glances up at the bell rope.

speaker: priest
text: When the founders came to this valley, they brought a relic with them, and they hung that bell to watch over it. Their mark was a tree under two moons; it is cut over the door, if you look, though the weather has nearly had it. The relic passed quietly down their line, until one night, years ago, it was lost, and the bell rang at midnight with no hand on the rope.

speaker: narrator
text: He sighs.

speaker: priest
text: And now I cannot even light a candle against the dark. I am out of matches, and I usually get them for free from the General Store. Could you bring me some?

speaker: narrator
text: The priest has asked you to help bring light to the chapel. Perhaps this small act will illuminate more than just the room for you.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest glances at the cold candle by the altar.

speaker: priest
text: Any luck with those matches, child? The General Store has always been kind to this chapel.

speaker: blacksmith
text: Saw it, did you? The deer? My grandfather swore by that deer. Said it only shows itself to them as the land has need of.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shopkeeper leans in.

text: Ah, you spoke to the priest? He does get through his matches. Here, take these for him, on the house. Tell him I said hello!

text: As you read the runes, you feel a connection to the ancient magic of nature. It does not wake in you the way the others did; this one you read, word by word, off the stone, and it feels like your own. You have learned the grow spell!

speaker: narrator
text: Carved beneath the runes, in a plainer hand, are words you can read:

speaker: narrator
text: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth.

speaker: narrator
text: You read them aloud. They mean nothing to you, and yet they stay with you.

speaker: narrator
text: It does not answer, not in words. It lifts its head toward the glowing stone, then dips it to you, slow and deliberate, as if in thanks. For a heartbeat the whole glade seems to breathe with it.

text: It lifts its head toward the glowing stone, then dips it to you, slow and deliberate, as if in thanks. For a heartbeat the whole glade seems to breathe with it.

speaker: narrator
text: grandmother's eyes widen as she sees the locket.

speaker: grandmother
text: This... this was your mother's. It came to her from me, and to me from my mother, all the way back to the founders, so the old ones said. I thought she took it with her when she left.

speaker: narrator
text: She closes her hand around it for a moment.

speaker: grandmother
text: She said it would keep you safe. And this... she wanted you to have this when you were old enough to understand its importance.

speaker: narrator
text: grandmother hands you a finely made travel cloak.

speaker: grandmother
text: May it protect you on your journeys, Elior.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest smiles.

speaker: priest
text: The chapel is brighter for your kindness, child. The founders would be glad of you.

speaker: narrator
text: Your resolve is strengthened, and you feel more prepared for the challenges that lie ahead on your journey.

speaker: narrator
text: The priest studies you for a long moment, then smiles.

speaker: priest
text: The blessing sits well on you. The founders' light has not gone out of their line after all. Go gently on the road.

speaker: narrator
text: You have explored every corner of Willowbrook. The village feels more like home, and you are ready for what lies ahead.

speaker: narrator
text: The main road leaving Willowbrook stretches beneath ancient oaks, their branches arching overhead like a living tunnel. The path is well-trodden, lined with wildflowers and scattered leaves. A merchant's cart creaks nearby, and the air is filled with the promise of adventure and the unknown. The road beckons, leading onward to new lands and new stories.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant offers a friendly nod.

speaker: merchant
text: You'll want news, if you're bound for Greendale. It's a sombre city this season: they say King Alden has fallen ill, and no physician can name the sickness. And the roads have gone bad besides. I passed a cart on its side by the hill road, and nobody with it. And it's not only your fields that are failing. I've seen crops gone grey in every valley from here to the capital, ever since the king took to his bed. Keep to the daylight, friend. Looking for something specific, or just browsing? If you have any fine jewelry, especially a shiny ring, I'm ready to exchange it for a pair of sturdy wandering boots. Failing that, my old mare threw a shoe on the hill road; a good iron horseshoe would do me nearly as well. Forgive me if I'm short, friend. I've not eaten since the hill road, and there's no inn this side of Greendale.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant's eyes widen as you hand over the shiny ring.

speaker: merchant
text: A fine piece! As promised, here are the wandering boots. They'll serve you well on the road to Greendale.

speaker: narrator
text: You have gathered all the items needed for your journey. With your preparations complete, you are ready to face whatever lies beyond Willowbrook.

speaker: narrator
text: The merchant grins.

speaker: merchant
text: You'll want news, if you're bound for Greendale. It's a sombre city this season: they say King Alden has fallen ill, and no physician can name the sickness. And the roads have gone bad besides. speaker: tilda
text: The water's clean! Was that you, Elior? No — don't tell me, you've that look about you. I've not had dough rise so light in a year.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira smiles, a deep wisdom in her eyes.

speaker: mira
text: You have done well, Elior. You have gathered your supplies, honed your magical skills, and prepared your spirit. You are ready.

speaker: narrator
text: She presents you with the Ancient Amulet.

speaker: mira
text: May this guide and protect you.

speaker: narrator
text: Then, more quietly:

speaker: mira
text: I knew your parents better than I have said. Once you are truly ready, I will tell you.

speaker: narrator
text: She holds your hand a moment longer, her tone serious.

speaker: mira
text: Your road leads to Greendale, Elior. Once there, show the amulet to no one lightly. Those who know what it is will find you.

speaker: mira
text: Trust in yourself, and remember: the fate of our village, or even more, may rest in your hands.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira turns the rune token over in her fingers, and the color drains from her face.

speaker: mira
text: This is a fouling sigil, Elior. Dropped into a well, it sours the water from below, slowly, so that no one thinks to look.

speaker: mira
text: The well did not sicken. Someone poisoned it on purpose.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her of the black-iron mechanism at the mill, and the twisted rune on its housing. She nods slowly.

speaker: mira
text: The same hand, then. The mill stands on old power, and that thing was drinking it. You did well to stop it.

speaker: mira
text: The cloaked stranger the villagers whisper about, perhaps. Whoever carried this was not here to spoil a well and leave. They were searching Willowbrook for something.

speaker: narrator
text: She is quiet a moment.

speaker: mira
text: Or for someone.

speaker: narrator
text: She presses the token back into your palm.

speaker: mira
text: Keep it close, and keep it hidden.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira named the token a fouling sigil: someone poisoned the well on purpose. Whoever carried it, perhaps the cloaked stranger the villagers whisper about, was searching Willowbrook for something, or for someone.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira looks at you kindly.

speaker: mira
text: The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. You have taken many already. Go now, and may your path be clear.

speaker: tilda
text: Mira's amulet... you're leaving, aren't you? Well. Don't you dare go without a proper send-off from the bakery. And mind you come home, love.

speaker: narrator
text: Her eyes fall on the amulet you carry, and she goes very still.

speaker: grandmother
text: So it's true, then. I knew this day would come; I only hoped it would come later. Come back to me, child.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother has walked all the way out from the village. She tugs the travel cloak straight on your shoulders.

speaker: grandmother
text: Wear your mother's cloak. She'd want you warm.

speaker: grandmother
text: The merchant showed me the ring he had of you. It was your mother's wedding ring, child. No, don't fret; she'd have given it for your boots in a heartbeat.

speaker: grandmother
text: Old Hemlock is telling the whole square how you found his Patches.

speaker: narrator
text: Her hand finds the amulet at your chest and closes around it.

speaker: grandmother
text: This was theirs, you know. Aren and Lysa's.

speaker: narrator
text: In all your years, you have never once heard her say their names.

speaker: grandmother
text: They gave it to Mira to keep for you, until you were ready. And someone has come to Willowbrook looking for it. Keep it hidden, child.

speaker: narrator
text: She kisses your brow, and turns for home before you can see her cry.

speaker: narrator
text: The map aligns with the landscape, revealing a hidden path that shortens the journey to Greendale. You tuck your parents' amulet beneath your mother's cloak, and set forth.
